      "snippet": "Short answer: no — not if it’s designed correctly.
Long answer (the important one): fail-closed must block mutation, not use.
Let’s lock this cleanly, because this is one of those places where systems quietly sabotage themselves.

The core distinction (this is the crux)
There are two very different things that can “fail”:

Using a tool

Letting a tool change the system

Fail-closed applies only to (2).
If fail-closed prevents (1), the system becomes brittle and self-defeating.
